title: news payload
description: Dated statements, each with the place it was read. The MINIMAL payload ticket 23 decided: id, date, source, statement, provenance.url and nothing else. There is no steep tag, no severity, no relevance, no subject and no component here, because every one of those is a judgement, and a judgement in this estate is a skill a human runs over the pool (the classify-and-judge skill) whose output is a grade-5 claim on the twin side, contestable and never a published fact. The entry map is `events`, a list keyed by `id`.

source.description: The pool this feed reads, verbatim.

events.description: The admitted events. A list, not a map: an event is a dated line in a log, not a slot somebody overwrites. bump.py keys it by `id`.

id.description: Stable across republishes: a claim on the twin side names this id as the signal it bound.

date.description: The date the thing was said, not the date it was read.

source.description: Who said it, as they are named at the URL.

statement.description: What was said, in the plainest terms that stay true to the source. Not a summary of what it means.

url.description: Where it was read. REQUIRED (ticket 23 answer point 2): an entry nobody can go and check is not an observation, and an invented headline has no URL, which is the mechanism that keeps a scenario out of this feed.

retrieved.description: The date the URL was read, where that differs from the event date.
